key_insight: Lineage inpainting uses the states of related cells to learn developmental dynamics that gene expression alone does not resolve.
engineering_relevance: Combining tree-structured context with generative modeling offers a framework for simulating multicellular development and proposing perturbation-response hypotheses.
method: Represent lineage context, including sister and cousin cells, with tree-structured transformers.
Use stochastic interpolants to generatively model cell-state dynamics across lineage trees.
Simulate counterfactual perturbations using a model fit on unperturbed development.
evidence_signal: On a lineage-traced transcriptional atlas of mouse embryogenesis, the model recovered transcriptional convergence events and produced perturbation predictions consistent with many observed phenotypes, including a single-cell Tbx5 knockout measurement.
watch_item: Counterfactual agreement is not universal; predictions from unperturbed training data require experimental validation.
paper_title: Learning developmental dynamics from lineage context
